details.description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B is an open, hybrid mixture-of-experts language model with 120 billion total parameters that activates about 12 billion parameters per token, built for cost-efficient multi-agent and agentic applications. AWS Bedrock lists it as launched March 11, 2026, with a 256K-token context window and up to 32K output tokens, and describes it as fully open, with public weights, training datasets and recipes for customization.
advantages: Activates only about 12B of its 120B total parameters through a hybrid mixture-of-experts design, which AWS's model card says delivers up to 7x higher inference throughput for agentic tasks.
Ships fully open, with public weights, datasets and training recipes rather than access limited to an API (AWS Bedrock model card).
Supports client-side tool calling on the bedrock-mantle endpoint (AWS Bedrock model card).
Provides a 256K-token context window described as giving agents long-term memory so they do not lose focus on long, multi-step tasks (AWS Bedrock model card).
Scores 83.73 on MMLU-Pro and 81.19 on LiveCodeBench, per NVIDIA's own model card (build.nvidia.com).
disadvantages: Text-only model: the Bedrock model card lists no support for image, audio or video input or output.
Server-side tool calling is not supported on the bedrock-mantle endpoint, only client-side tool calling (AWS Bedrock model card).
use_cases: Long, multi-step reasoning tasks that need extended context
Cost- and compute-efficient text inference at scale

sources.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B model card - Amazon Bedrock

notes: NVIDIA's own build.nvidia.com model page (without the /modelcard suffix the AWS page links to) loads and lists benchmark scores and a license/modality summary; the /modelcard sub-route itself is still JS-rendered/empty, and the Hugging Face card still returns 401. Added 5 accuracy-style benchmark scores from that page; excluded Arena-Hard-V2 as an arena/win-rate score, not an accuracy score. That page also states a 1-million-token 'maximum context length', which conflicts with AWS Bedrock's 256K and the catalog's max_input_tokens fact of 256000 -- kept the catalog value per the facts-are-authoritative rule. Removed the 'bedrock-runtime' half of the tool-calling advantage: the Bedrock model card's per-endpoint feature table lists client-side tool calling only under bedrock-mantle features; the bedrock-runtime features table does not mention tool calling at all. Catalog's max_output_tokens facts list both 32000 and 32768; the source only states '32K', which does not resolve which is exact, so I kept the catalog values as-is.
